documents.t: Open a filament to switch between Colors, Spools, Usage, and History. Its color rows summarize stock and consumption. Stock numbers describe registered inventory, so keep spool loading, weights, and corrections current.
Feed units describe the printer's physical material paths. Each has slots where tracked spools can be loaded. Open the printer's feed-unit card to inspect and manage them.

Bambu printers expose AMS positions and external spool paths according to their hardware. The U1 exposes one four-slot toolhead unit, T1–T4, with each slot feeding its corresponding head. The spool record and the printer's reported material are separate. Check both when troubleshooting.

Use Add reloader to describe an external reloader's spool positions. Choose its physical feeding slot and whether it replaces an existing external spool port. The add flow defaults to two slots and an available external port. If replacing a port with a registered spool, transfer it to the selected reloader slot or return it to storage. Occupied destinations are refused. Only one active reloader may replace the same port.

The feeding slot is the spool position actually supplying the printer. Change it when the physical path changes. A selection can exist even when the filament has not been registered, but that does not satisfy production's tracked-spool requirement. Only the selected reloader slot supplies material for job matching. Compatible standby spools can count toward the stock available to continue the print. Port detection reports the replaced printer port. It does not report a separate sensor for each standby slot. If recorded usage finishes a spool, OpenFarm can select another loaded spool in the same reloader as estimated continuation. Check the physical reloader. The record does not confirm that the hardware switched spools successfully.

Removing a reloader returns its tracked spools to storage and keeps their weights and history. OpenFarm archives the reloader, and the original external port becomes available again. Adding it again creates a new unit.
One spool record represents one physical roll. Its states are In storage → Using → Finished. OpenFarm keeps its usage history through these changes.

Use Add spools from the filament workflow. Enter one line per filament/color and roll specification, then set its quantity. Shared purchase details such as supplier, order, and date are entered once for the batch. Set the spool weight, known remaining filament for a partly used roll, and price per spool when known. Full identical rolls can appear grouped on the shelf; expand the group to inspect individual labels.

Physically load the spool into the intended printer feed path. Choose Load spool and select the matching printer, feed unit, and slot. Check that the slot shows the intended inventory record and material. Unload returns the record to storage without discarding its remaining weight. Registration does not physically move filament. A printer's reported material alone does not establish tracked inventory.

OpenFarm links each job's filament to a loaded spool. It estimates consumption from the file sent to the printer. For completed prints, OpenFarm deducts the estimated usage. For stopped prints, it uses available layer or progress information. Object exclusions affect the estimate. Filament use is not simply proportional to the number of good units produced. These are estimates, not scale measurements. Prints started outside OpenFarm can also be tracked when the server can recover their file and spool mapping.

Open a spool for its weight and history. Use Record usage for adjustments such as purging, test extrusion, or drift. Correct the remaining amount when a measured weight is more reliable. If OpenFarm cannot identify a spool or estimate, the print appears under Action required. Open the print and assign a spool or resolve the missing usage information where the controls are available. Make a manual adjustment if necessary. Do not deduct the same usage twice. Use Finish when the roll is exhausted. Feed units and reloaders explains how OpenFarm selects continuation spools.
The production image includes default settings. To change them, enter overrides in .env next to your Compose file. ASP.NET setting names use double underscores, such as Seed__AdminPassword.

Setting Purpose POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB Initialize the bundled PostgreSQL database on its first start. Database__Host Database hostname or address. The supplied host-network configuration uses 127.0.0.1. Database__Port PostgreSQL port, normally 5432. ConnectionStrings__Default Optional full connection string; takes precedence over the Database__* settings. Seed__AdminUsername, Seed__AdminEmail, Seed__AdminPassword First administrator, created only if needed. ORIGIN Optional deployment override for Settings → Server → Public URL. Locks the field while set. MCP_MODE Optional deployment override: Disabled, AccessTokens, or SignIn. Locks MCP mode in settings. MCP_ENABLED Optional deployment override. true enables MCP; false disables all MCP and OAuth access. Unset leaves control in Settings. OAUTH_ENABLED Legacy upgrade setting. An explicit true imports sign-in mode once when installation settings are first created. Requires HTTPS ORIGIN. OAuth__RegisterPermitLimit, OAuth__PermitLimit Sign-in requests allowed per minute from one address: app registrations (default 10) and other sign-in requests (default 60). Jwt__SigningKey Optional token signing key. If omitted, OpenFarm generates one and saves it under /data/keys. DataProtection__CertificatePath, DataProtection__CertificatePassword Optional PKCS#12 certificate protecting stored printer-credential encryption keys at rest. PUID, PGID, TZ Data ownership and log time zone. Slicing__MaxConcurrentSlicingOperations Maximum number of slicing operations that can run at the same time. Default: 2. Dispatch__MaxConcurrent Maximum number of printers that can receive a job at the same time (slicing, upload and start). Default: 3. 1 sends one job at a time. Use deploy/.env.example for the current supported examples. Farm currency and prices are configured in the application under Settings.

Set the Public URL under Settings → Server. For a deployment-controlled HTTPS hostname or Cloudflare Tunnel, you can instead set: ORIGIN=https://farm.example.com Route the entire hostname, including /api and /hubs, to http://<server-ip>:6868. The proxy must allow WebSocket connections for live updates. No separate frontend build or API hostname is needed. ORIGIN must contain a scheme and hostname, with an optional port. Do not include a path other than /, a query, a fragment, or credentials. An invalid value stops startup. Apply changed environment settings by recreating the application: docker compose up -d --force-recreate openfarm With an HTTPS origin, refresh cookies use the Secure attribute, even if the proxy connects to OpenFarm over HTTP. Sign in through that HTTPS hostname. Those cookies do not work for direct HTTP sign-in over the LAN. For trusted local HTTP hosting, leave the saved public URL blank and omit ORIGIN. Removing an override does not clear the saved URL.

MCP is disabled by default. Administrators can enable Access tokens only or Sign-in and access tokens under Settings → Integrations. The second mode requires an HTTPS public URL, except for localhost development. Changes in Settings apply without restarting. For automated deployments, use: ORIGIN=https://farm.example.com MCP_MODE=SignIn ORIGIN overrides the saved public URL. MCP_MODE overrides the saved mode. MCP_ENABLED=true enables access tokens when the saved mode is disabled; otherwise it keeps the enabled mode. Use MCP_MODE=SignIn to select OAuth. MCP_ENABLED=false disables every mode. An explicit availability or mode override makes the MCP control read-only. Leave both unset to manage MCP in Settings. Do not combine MCP_ENABLED=true with MCP_MODE=Disabled. Environment changes require recreating the application. Changing deployment policy invalidates existing signed-in apps and pending connections on startup. Keep the deployment settings consistent when replacing the application instance. The public URL supplies sign-in addresses and token identity. OpenFarm does not derive them from request hosts or forwarded headers. Route /mcp, /oauth/ and /.well-known/ to OpenFarm. Do not place a login wall in front of discovery or /oauth/token. The request limits count the address that connects to OpenFarm. Behind a proxy, assistants can share one count. Adjust OAuth__PermitLimit if necessary.

When the new installation settings are first created, an explicit OAUTH_ENABLED=true and valid ORIGIN preserve sign-in and existing app grants. This import runs once. Later UI changes are not overwritten by the legacy flag. Remove OAUTH_ENABLED after upgrading; use MCP_MODE for continued deployment control. Installations that previously used token-only MCP must enable MCP after upgrading. Personal access tokens retain their REST access. Changing the public URL or MCP mode in settings invalidates app grants and pending authorizations; users must reconnect their signed-in assistants. Setup steps: AI assistants.

Preserve /data/keys with the database and part files. Losing Data Protection keys makes saved printer credentials unreadable. Replacing the signing key invalidates existing login tokens. See Upgrades and backups before moving an installation.
Use the repository's production Compose files to run OpenFarm and PostgreSQL on a Linux host. The supplied configuration uses host networking so OpenFarm can discover printers on the LAN.

Docker Engine and the Compose plugin. A host that can reach your printers' LAN addresses. Persistent storage for the database and application data. Port 6868 available for the web application and 5432 for PostgreSQL with the supplied host-network layout. The released image is built for linux/amd64. Do not assume an ARM image is available.

Create a directory for the installation. Download these two repository files into it: deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml, saved as docker-compose.yml. deploy/.env.example, saved as .env. If you already have the repository checked out: mkdir -p openfarm-install cp deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml openfarm-install/docker-compose.yml cp deploy/.env.example openfarm-install/.env cd openfarm-install Edit .env before the first start: POSTGRES_USER=openfarm POSTGRES_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-strong-database-password POSTGRES_DB=openfarm Database__Host=127.0.0.1 Seed__AdminUsername=admin Seed__AdminPassword=replace-with-a-strong-admin-password Make sure the configured password matches the database password. PostgreSQL uses initialization variables only when it creates a new volume. The current source Compose file puts OpenFarm on the host network but leaves PostgreSQL on a private container network. Add this inside its existing postgres service so Database__Host=127.0.0.1 can reach it: ports: - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432" Keep the loopback address so the database port is not published to the LAN. If PostgreSQL already runs on the host, configure that database instead of starting a second server on the same port.

docker compose up -d docker compose logs --tail=100 openfarm On startup, OpenFarm applies database migrations, creates the first administrator account, and imports the bundled slicer profiles. Open http://<server-ip>:6868 and sign in with the configured administrator credentials. If you omitted Seed__AdminPassword, the initial password is admin-openfarm. Change it before allowing other people to reach the installation. Seed settings do not reset an existing account's password.

The supplied Compose file uses named volumes data and postgres. Application data is mounted at /data and includes part files and cryptographic keys. Keep both volumes when recreating containers. Host networking supports Bambu SSDP and Snapmaker mDNS discovery. The host's firewall controls which network connections can reach OpenFarm. Restrict database access to the OpenFarm host. If multicast discovery is unavailable with your container network setup, add printers by IP address. One application instance Run exactly one OpenFarm application instance per installation. Do not scale the service or run overlapping application containers against the same database during an upgrade. Continue with Configuration, then the Quick start.
Back up PostgreSQL and the application data volume as one recovery set. A database alone does not contain the uploaded files or keys needed to use stored printer credentials.

For the supplied production Compose file, run these commands from its directory. Let active prints finish first when possible. Pause new work before you stop the application. Stopping OpenFarm keeps files and database records consistent during the backup. backup_dir="backups/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)" mkdir -p "$backup_dir" docker compose stop openfarm docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c 'pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" "${POSTGRES_DB:-$POSTGRES_USER}"' > "$backup_dir/openfarm.sql" Confirm the dump succeeded before continuing. Copy the stopped application's /data out of its container, which remains available after stopping: docker compose cp openfarm:/data "$backup_dir/application-data" docker compose start openfarm Store the SQL dump, copied data (including keys/), Compose file, .env, and encryption certificates together in a secure location. If a backup step fails, keep previous backups. Restart the application when appropriate. Test recovery on a separate, isolated installation before you rely on the backup.

The MCP settings update adds installation settings to the database. Token-only MCP installations must enable Access tokens only under Settings → Integrations after upgrading. Existing REST tokens remain valid. An explicit legacy OAUTH_ENABLED=true with a valid ORIGIN preserves sign-in on the first upgrade. See MCP configuration. After taking a backup: docker compose pull docker compose stop openfarm docker compose up -d openfarm docker compose logs --tail=100 openfarm Migrations run on startup. Keep the existing project directory and project name so Compose reuses the same named volumes. To control when you upgrade, use a specific release image tag instead of latest. Only one application instance can use the database. Expect brief downtime. Do not run overlapping instances during an upgrade.

Prepare an isolated installation with the application version that matches the backup. Keep OpenFarm stopped and start PostgreSQL only. Restore the dump into an empty database using its configured owner. Restore the contents of the saved application data to the volume mounted at /data. Restore the matching configuration and certificates. Check file ownership against PUID and PGID. Verify that the original encryption keys are present. Start one OpenFarm application instance. Inspect the logs. Confirm sign-in, files, printer credentials, and queued work before returning the farm to use. Rollback requires a compatible application and database schema. Starting an old image against a migrated database is not a restore strategy. Do not use docker compose down -v on an installation whose data you need to keep.
An assembly is a reusable product definition. It contains at least one part or sub-assembly with quantities. Creating one does not create print jobs.

Open Assemblies → Add assembly. Set the name and description. In Structure, use Add part or assembly and set quantities per finished assembly. Add additional Cost items such as hardware, packaging, labor, or shipping as needed. Save the assembly. For nested assemblies, OpenFarm multiplies component quantities through each level. It prevents circular definitions, such as an assembly containing itself. The library selection list can find items across folders. Moving a record to another folder does not change its bill of materials (BOM) references.

For complete products, create a run and request the assembly in sets. OpenFarm expands the whole batch and totals each printed part before splitting it into plate jobs. It does not multiply the rounded plate count for one set by the number of sets. The assembly's direct Print action lets you enter whole-plate counts for each printed component. Use a run's set quantity when you need an exact number of complete products. Non-printed cost items contribute estimated costs, not printer output or stock reservations. A run does not purchase or consume cost-catalog inventory.

The assembly page's Build estimate combines printed materials, configured printer costs, additional costs, and applicable allowances. The Pricing section calculates sale-price estimates against fee profiles. See Costs and pricing. To include packaging or labor for a standalone part, create an assembly containing that part. If inputs are missing, the cost estimate remains partial or unknown.
Parts hold the files and requirements used to create jobs. Start from Parts → Add part.

You can upload a project 3MF, a sliced .gcode.3mf, and raw .gcode / .gco / .g files. STL and geometry-only 3MF files are refused: they carry no machine, process, or plate to slice with. The complete upload request has a 500 MiB limit. Leave space for the form data sent with the file. A supported file extension does not guarantee readable metadata or compatibility with every printer. Use a file prepared for the intended printer; raw G-code cannot safely become a different machine's toolpath just by changing a profile. See When profiles apply for the file decision tree and the separate rules for library estimates, production slicing, and already-sliced jobs.

Upload or drop a file. Set its name and tags. Wait for background processing to finish. Review the extracted plates, material requirements, nozzle, quantity, and estimates. For a multi-plate file, select the plates to save. Complete missing requirements. Choose Production filament for each material line: the file color (default), any color of the material, any color of one filament, or one color. Confirm the review to save the part records. For sliced 3MF and G-code, OpenFarm reads estimates stored in the file. For unsliced project 3MF, it can calculate estimates from embedded settings or supported named presets. You can review and save a project 3MF without estimates. Unknown time or filament weight stays unknown. It does not become zero.

An Incomplete part can be kept in the library while you fill gaps. Ready to print indicates complete part requirements, while actual dispatch still depends on printer matching. If OpenFarm recognizes the object quantity, you cannot edit it. For files with unknown quantities, you can enter a whole-plate quantity manually. That value does not enable object skipping. Exact quantities require verified object identifiers in the file. See Outcomes and recovery.

Edit the saved details and save your changes. File replacement and reprocessing each have a separate review step. They keep the part's saved slicer and exact version unless you select another slicer. Changing the farm default does not update existing parts. Finite queued jobs retain their captured production inputs. Changing a part does not rewrite running jobs or recorded material consumption.

Use folders, tags, search, and the Details / Thumbnails switch. Move items with Move to or drag them to a supported destination. Folders organize records; they do not set a manual item order. You can remove only empty folders. Moving a part does not change the assemblies that use it.

A file carries its own machine, process, and plate. OpenFarm does not choose them. A project 3MF needs slicing, and the slicer uses the settings saved in the project. Supported sliced 3MF and raw G-code already contain toolpaths. OpenFarm chooses only the filament profile for each spool, and checks that the file fits the destination printer. There are two separate stages: Library processing reads the uploaded file and, when supported, calculates estimates. It does not select settings from your connected printers or loaded spools. Production file preparation checks the destination printer and its loaded spools. If slicing is needed, OpenFarm slices the project with its own settings and the part's saved slicer engine and exact version. The saved engine and version are called the slicer pin. Pinning a job to a printer is a separate choice. A successful estimate or Ready to print part does not guarantee that a particular printer can take the job. Printer matching still applies.

Profile Where it comes from Role when slicing Printer / machine The project file. Machine settings, including machine G-code and nozzle configuration. OpenFarm checks that the file names the destination printer's model, and checks the connected printer's nozzle report. Process The project file. Layer height, walls, infill, and support settings. Filament Edit the filament → assign a profile for the printer brand, model, and nozzle size. A color can override this assignment. Material settings for the tracked spool selected for each required material and color. Build plate The project file names its plate. Edit the printer to set the plate on its bed. A job goes only to a printer whose plate matches the file's plate. A printer record describes physical hardware. A spool record tracks a physical roll of filament. A filament profile contains material settings for the slicer. Selecting a profile does not change the physical nozzle, plate, or material.

The .3mf extension alone does not answer this question. A 3MF archive can contain geometry, project settings, or sliced toolpaths. A project can also retain geometry and settings after slicing. File contents OpenFarm's route STL Refused. It carries no machine, process, or plate. Geometry-only 3MF Refused. It has no project settings. Save it as a project from OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio. Project 3MF No supported plate G-code, but contains project settings; needs production slicing even if OpenFarm successfully estimates it. Sliced 3MF, often named .gcode.3mf Contains a supported Metadata/plate_*.gcode entry. OpenFarm treats the upload as already sliced, even if it also contains project settings and models. Raw .gcode, .gco, or .g Already sliced. OpenFarm looks inside the 3MF archive for supported plate G-code. The .gcode.3mf filename alone does not select the file's processing route. Other vendors' 3MF layouts are not automatically supported. OpenFarm can reject malformed or unsupported files. Unreadable or conflicting metadata can leave requirements or estimates unknown. If an archive contains supported plate G-code, OpenFarm processes the upload as already sliced. This also applies to archives that mix sliced and unsliced plates. OpenFarm does not automatically slice the remaining plates. A requested plate must have usable sliced output. For background on the format, Prusa's Saving projects as 3MF explains why a project can carry settings and modifiers as well as geometry. OpenFarm's own supported entries determine its behavior.
documents.s: Which kind of file did I upload?

documents.t: Library estimates do not use the fleet's selected machine and process profiles or the inventory's filament-profile assignments. There is no separate farm estimation profile to configure. Uploaded file Source of library time and weight estimates Are production profiles applied? Supported unsliced project 3MF OpenFarm first runs the selected slicer with the project's embedded settings. See the restricted retry below. No; the destination printer and loaded spools are not selected here. Sliced 3MF or raw G-code Metadata already present in the file. OpenFarm does not run the slicer to recalculate it. No. Missing time or weight stays unknown. It does not become zero. If an estimate fails, you can still save a part after reviewing its requirements. Production still needs complete requirements.

OpenFarm can estimate recognized OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio projects from their embedded settings. The settings must be usable, and the selected slicer engine and version must be available. This estimation mode excludes Bambu Studio 2.7.1 on macOS. It does not support Prusa or Cura project settings. The first attempt loads the project without external machine, process, or filament preset files. A second attempt is available only for specific validation, version, or modified-machine errors. For this second attempt, OpenFarm: Reads the machine, process, and filament preset names and the build plate stored in the project. Looks up each preset by name in the selected engine's exact version catalog. Each name must have exactly one match. Checks that the build plate is recognized and the matched presets are compatible. Retries with those catalog presets. This retry replaces the project's global preset settings. It does not reproduce custom edits to those presets. Project geometry and local settings remain inputs to the slicer. The retry requires one distinct nonblank filament preset name. Several slots can share that name. A project with several different filament presets can succeed on the first attempt. It cannot use this retry. Missing presets, multiple matches, or another slicing failure leave the estimate unavailable. This retry does not select your fleet's production profiles. Production dispatch does not use this retry as a fallback.
documents.s: Project settings and the named-preset retry

documents.t: For an unsliced upload, the toolpath generated for estimation is temporary. OpenFarm saves the estimates and thumbnails, then discards that toolpath. It slices the stored source again when preparing a production job.
documents.s: Estimating does not make the source file pre-sliced

documents.t: Direct part printing, assembly printing, runs with fixed quantities, and continuous backfill all create queue work. They use the same file preparation and dispatch checks. Pinning a job restricts it to one printer. It does not bypass those checks.
documents.s: When a job is prepared for a printer

documents.t: For each destination printer, OpenFarm: Checks that the job's requirements are complete and current printer reports confirm the nozzle size. Checks that the file names the destination printer's model and the plate on the printer's bed. A mismatch blocks the job. Finds matching tracked spools on active feed paths. Selects each spool's filament-profile assignment for that printer hardware and nozzle size. A color override takes priority over the filament default. Requires the job's exact slicer engine and version pin. Finds the compatible filament presets and their inherited settings in the pinned catalog. Checks each required filament separately, including its bed-temperature setting for the file's plate. Slices the part's selected project plate with the project's own machine and process settings. OpenFarm loads only the filament presets over them. Rechecks the current configuration and stock before sending. If a check or slicing fails, OpenFarm sends nothing. A profile constraint saved on a part or job must agree with the loaded spool's assignment. It cannot select a replacement preset. Spools in storage or on another printer are not fallbacks. A project saved by a newer slicer than the pinned version can fail to slice. OpenFarm blocks the job. It does not substitute other presets. Setting source Used to generate the production file? The project's machine, process, and plate settings Yes. They are the file's own settings. Filament-profile assignments for the selected tracked spools Yes, after matching and compatibility checks, for each required filament slot. They take priority over the project's filament presets. Destination printer's selected build plate Checked, not applied. The file's plate must equal it. Project geometry, placement, painting, modifiers, and object or part settings Yes. The slicer reads them from the project. The OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio command-line interfaces (CLIs) give external filament presets priority over project-level filament settings. See the loading priority in the OrcaSlicer 2.3.1 CLI implementation and Bambu Studio 2.7.1 CLI implementation. For multi-color projects, OpenFarm matches each project slot to a job line by its detected material and color. It loads the matched filament profile for each slot, in slot order. A slot known to be unused on that plate needs no separate job line. If a used slot has no match, OpenFarm blocks the job. It does not keep an embedded filament preset as a substitute. Production profile matching supports OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio. A SuperSlicer CLI adapter exists in the code, but it does not support these profile catalogs. It cannot bypass a missing or incompatible profile.
documents.s: Project 3MF: generate a new production file

documents.t: OpenFarm does not re-slice these files or apply any profile to their toolpaths. Configuration What happens for an already-sliced job? Machine and process Not used. The toolpaths keep the settings of the original slice. Filament-profile assignments Required and validated for the loaded, tracked spools. OpenFarm checks material, nozzle, and saved profile constraints. It does not replace toolpath settings such as temperature, flow, or cooling. Build plate Checked. The file must name the plate on the destination printer's bed. A different or missing plate blocks the job. Part's slicer pin No slicer is run. OpenFarm does not look up these validation assignments in a pinned slicer catalog. For real supported printers, the file must declare a recognizable target printer model matching the destination, and the plate on the printer's bed. A missing or unrecognized model or plate, a different model, or a different plate blocks the job. These checks do not apply to the simulator. They apply to project 3MF files too. Entering a missing nozzle or material requirement manually does not add a missing printer-model or plate declaration to the file. Temperatures, speeds, layer height, supports, and other toolpath choices remain those of the original slice. Choosing another spool color changes which physical stock can match the job. It does not rewrite the file's slicing settings. Existing toolpaths can still need execution preparation OpenFarm can still prepare the file for a partial plate or supported object skipping. It can also package or adapt the file for the printer's protocol. The uploaded bytes can therefore differ from the stored file. These operations do not apply slicing profiles. See Outcomes and recovery.
documents.s: Sliced 3MF and raw G-code: keep the existing toolpaths

documents.t: Downloading a part's original file returns the stored upload without applying profiles. It does not export the temporary library-estimation result. A job file download returns the file saved for that job, if available. Otherwise, OpenFarm prepares a production file as described above. This requires an assigned or pinned target printer. Downloading a saved job file does not slice it again with today's profiles. OpenFarm can observe a print started outside its queue. This is a printer-started print. Observing it does not cause OpenFarm to slice it or apply profile settings.
documents.s: Original downloads, job downloads, and printer-started prints

documents.t: This section applies when OpenFarm slices a production file. It concerns the filament profile, the only profile OpenFarm resolves. A selected profile can come from a different catalog than the part's pinned slicer: Saved choice Resolution for production slicing System preset already in the pinned engine and version Use that preset. System preset from another version of the same engine Find a match by vendor and external preset ID. A renamed preset can match. Without an ID, use vendor and name. System preset from the other supported engine Require an exact match by external ID, vendor, and name. A similar display name is insufficient. User preset made for the pinned engine Use the user preset. Match its inherited system presets to the pinned catalog. User preset from another engine Block. OpenFarm blocks slicing if a preset is missing, has multiple matches, or is incompatible. It also blocks missing catalogs, unavailable slicers, and inherited presets or templates that it cannot load. It does not substitute a similar preset, another engine, or a newer version.
documents.s: Which version of a profile is used?

documents.t: Change Effect Change the farm default slicer Changes the default for new processing and the catalog shown in profile lists. Existing parts and jobs keep their pins. Replace or reprocess a project 3MF Keeps its current pin unless you choose another slicer. A part without a pin can use the farm default. Reads requirements and estimates again using the applicable route above. Reprocess a sliced file Reads its metadata again. Does not regenerate toolpaths with your current profiles. Change the printer's build plate, or a filament assignment OpenFarm checks the new configuration on the next production preparation, according to the file route. Saved library estimates stay unchanged. Change settings or loaded spools while a file is being generated Dispatch checks fresh state again. A configuration mismatch stops the send and leaves the job for retry. Edit a library part after jobs with fixed quantities were queued Those jobs keep their saved source inputs and pin. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings and spool assignments. Continuous backfill can use the updated part before dispatch. To keep an external slicer's toolpaths, upload its supported sliced output. To have OpenFarm slice for you, upload a project 3MF. It uses the project's own machine and process settings. Either route still needs a file made for the destination printer's model and plate, and compatible hardware, material, and filament configuration.
documents.s: What happens after I change something?

documents.t: Profiles are saved slicer settings, also called presets. They are separate from physical printer and spool records. The Profiles page has separate catalogs for machine, process, and filament profiles. See When profiles apply for the rules for project 3MF, sliced 3MF, and G-code.

The production image includes the slicers listed in the repository manifest. On startup, OpenFarm imports their system profiles. Each slicer engine and version has its own catalog. Choose the farm's default slicer engine and exact version under Settings → Slicing defaults. This determines the catalog shown in selection lists and the default for new file processing. Existing parts keep their saved engine and version, called the slicer pin.

Open Profiles → Import profiles. The UI accepts .zip, .orca_printer, .orca_filament, .bbscfg, and .bbsflmt bundles, with a 20 MiB request body limit. Upload the bundle. Review the machine and filament presets found in it. Select the presets to import. Confirm the import. OpenFarm saves nothing before confirmation. A preset embedded in a project is not necessarily available as an import.

The file carries its machine, process, and plate. The printer sets the plate on its bed. The filament assigns a profile for each printer model and nozzle size. A color can override that assignment. The part keeps its saved slicer engine and exact version for file processing and production slicing. Unsliced multi-color projects need compatible profiles for every required material slot. Pre-sliced files keep their toolpaths and must match the model they declare.

If a job needs slicing, OpenFarm finds the selected presets in the part's pinned slicer catalog. A matching system preset can come from another supported catalog. A user preset from another slicer engine is blocked. Missing profiles, multiple matches, unloaded catalogs, and incompatible presets stop the job. OpenFarm does not substitute another preset. Already-sliced files skip this catalog matching. They still require filament-profile assignments for loaded spools. Open Job diagnosis to see the requirement and a link to the relevant settings. If profiles are missing after a local setup, run the profile-import step in Local development. Find the cause of a compatibility failure before changing the slicer pin.
The Dashboard shows camera tiles, current prints, and printer warnings. Use it to find machines that need attention. Open the printer or job page to use its controls.

Each browser tab uses one live connection for printer and job updates. OpenFarm refreshes camera images while they are visible. The images are periodic snapshots, not video recordings. If a camera image stops updating, check the camera connection separately from MQTT or Moonraker status. If all live updates stop, check the browser connection and the reverse proxy's WebSocket support for /hubs/farm.

Inspect and remove the printed output before you mark the printer ready. A finished tile means you must inspect and clear the bed. It does not confirm that every unit is acceptable. See Outcomes and recovery for output confirmation and replacements.

Users with audit access can open Audit log under Administration. The table shows when a change happened, who made it, the affected record, and what changed. Filter by person, channel, token or app, record type, action, or date range. Select Everything to see all recorded changes. Select Tokens and apps to focus on changes made through those channels. Type groups the record type and action filters. Date opens the From and To controls. Open an entry to inspect its recorded field values before and after the change. The entry also shows other changes from the same request. Actor and record names are saved with new entries. Historical entries can have missing names or field details. Printer status reports and alert changes remain in Recent activity on each printer page. Operator actions, such as Mark ready, also appear in the audit log. Automatic changes to jobs, production, and inventory identify System as the actor. The audit log is not the source for utilization hours. Stats uses dedicated printer-activity history and print records, including gaps when the server could not observe a machine.
Create a maintenance task once and assign it to printers. Each assigned printer has its own service cycle.

Open Maintenance → Add task. Give the task a name and at least one positive interval: days, print hours, or print count. Choose a warning threshold and the printers to enroll. Save the task. Existing templates can also be added from a printer's maintenance card using Add tasks. Seeded tasks are editable templates. Choose intervals based on the printer and operating conditions. Editing a shared task changes the definition for every enrolled printer.

If a task has several intervals, it becomes due when the first interval is reached. The default warning threshold is 80%. Due soon warns before an interval is reached. Overdue means at least one interval has been reached. Hours use recorded printer activity and print durations. A ≥ indicator means actual hours can be higher because OpenFarm could not track some time. Failed prints, cancelled prints, and observed printer-started prints can also contribute to wear. Overdue maintenance currently warns only; it does not block automatic dispatch. Pause or otherwise manage work before physically servicing a printer.

After you complete the service, choose Mark done. Add a note if necessary. A service date cannot be in the future or before the current cycle began. OpenFarm records the signed-in user as the person who did the service. Use Set last done to record service completed before OpenFarm began tracking it. Include known usage since that service. OpenFarm keeps the history if you later remove the task or printer. The page has views for tasks needing attention, all tasks, task definitions, and history. Recording completed service requires different permissions from managing or removing task definitions.
Open Stats to review the farm over a selected date range and compare it with the preceding equivalent period.

Figure Interpretation Prints and success Includes ended prints that actually started. Success rate is completed prints divided by all completed, failed, and cancelled attempts. Printer time Recorded periods of printing, not-ready, paused, idle, and offline status. Not-ready time covers both a finished plate waiting to be cleared and a printer you marked not ready. Unobserved time appears as no data. Utilization Printing hours divided by observed hours. Offline time is observed; unknown time is excluded. Queue wait Time from job creation to start, summarized for jobs that started in the range. Filament and waste Compares recorded or estimated material use for completed work with material use for failed and cancelled work. Units made Stats uses the recorded plate quantities of completed jobs. Use job and run outcome details to verify the exact accepted output.

The date range uses local days in the browser's time zone. The API accepts an IANA time zone and supports up to 366 days. OpenFarm groups prints by their end date, not their queue date. Time comes from printer activity. Output comes from print records. A print that has not ended does not contribute a completed duration. Server downtime can leave periods with no data. OpenFarm cannot reconstruct every print that started and ended while the server was offline.

OpenFarm estimates material use from files and observed print progress. Recorded material cost uses the price saved when OpenFarm deducted the usage. Later catalog price changes do not change that recorded cost. Missing prices or deductions can leave the report incomplete. Use the filament's Usage / History, spool history, and Action required print entries to investigate discrepancies. These reports do not measure filament on a scale or record sales revenue.
The normal workflow is: define a part, load a compatible spool, request output, and let a ready printer take the resulting job.

Record What it represents Part A saved source file or selected plate, its print requirements, and production filament choices. Assembly A product definition containing parts and sub-assemblies with quantities. Cost items can be added separately. Filament and color A catalog material identity and its color variants, prices, and profile assignments. Spool A physical roll, with remaining weight, purchase details, and usage history. Feed unit and slot The printer's material path: AMS, external spool, toolheads, or a configured reloader. A tracked spool is loaded into a slot. Profile Slicer settings for a machine, process, or filament. Profiles are separate from physical inventory.

Production demand describes what you want to make. It can exist without a run. A print job is one attempt to print a plate. OpenFarm assigns it automatically, or you pin it to a specific printer. A run groups a fixed production target so you can track an order or batch. Parts can be requested in whole plates or unit targets; assemblies in a run are requested in complete sets. Exact unit targets can require a partial final plate, which needs reliable object identities. Runs explains this planning flow. Continuous backfill repeatedly makes whole plates when compatible printers are ready, after jobs with fixed quantities. You can pause it and limit how many printers it uses at the same time.

A saved part can be incomplete. A complete part can still have no matching printer. A matching printer can be busy or waiting for bed clearance. Production checks connectivity, availability, confirmed nozzle sizes, file compatibility, tracked loaded spools, profiles, and stock where estimates are known. Use Job diagnosis to see which layer is blocking work.

Jobs with fixed quantities save their production inputs when queued. Running jobs keep those saved inputs. Backfill uses current part inputs until OpenFarm prepares and sends the job. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings before sending. Editing a library record does not rewrite a completed print's material history. Requeue uses retained production inputs; Outcomes and recovery covers the limits.

Term Meaning in these guides Toolpath The movement and extrusion instructions generated by a slicer. G-code contains toolpaths. Metadata Information stored with a file, such as its material, nozzle size, or estimated print time. Preset or profile A saved set of slicer settings. OpenFarm groups profiles into catalogs by slicer and version. Slicer pin The slicer engine and exact version saved for a part. It is separate from pinning a job to a printer. Pinned printer The only printer that a job is allowed to use. The job must still pass compatibility checks. Production snapshot The source file reference, requirements, and slicer selection saved for a job. Current printer settings and loaded spools are still checked. Object identity An identifier in the file that lets OpenFarm distinguish a printable object for quantity checks or object skipping. Dispatch The process of preparing a job and sending it to a printer.
OpenFarm manages a 3D print farm from one web application. You run it on your own server, keep the database and files, and connect directly to supported printers on your LAN.

Monitor the fleet, printer status, cameras, and current work. Track filament colors, physical spools, loaded slots, usage, and estimated material costs. Store parts, import slicer profiles, and build nested assemblies. Queue plates directly, plan finite runs, and fill spare capacity with continuous backfill. Diagnose why a printer cannot take a job, then follow the link to its configuration. Track maintenance, production statistics, cost estimates, and product pricing. Give team members specific permissions and issue scoped API tokens.

Each installation serves one farm. Run one application instance with PostgreSQL. That instance manages printer connections and sends jobs to printers. You can use the browser remotely, but the server must have network access to the printers. See Installation for deployment and Supported printers for the actual model catalog.

The application groups daily work under Operate and reusable records under Library. Settings and account administration are separate. Start with the Quick start, then read Key concepts when you need to understand how parts, spools, jobs, and runs relate.
Bambu printers connect directly over the LAN. OpenFarm does not ask for a Bambu Cloud account.

Confirm the model is in the supported catalog. Enable LAN-only access and Developer Mode where required by the printer's firmware. Find its IP address, serial number, and LAN access code in the printer settings. Make sure the OpenFarm server can reach the printer. Enabling LAN-only mode changes how you use the printer with Bambu Cloud and its apps.

Open Printers → Add printer. Select the discovered printer. For manual entry, set the brand, model, IP address, and serial number. Enter a name and the LAN access code. Add the printer. OpenFarm verifies the connection before saving the printer. Credentials stay encrypted on the server. Enter or replace them from the printer's add/edit page.

Wait for the connected printer to report its nozzle size. Edit the printer and select the build plate on the bed. Register the physical spools and assign compatible filament profiles. Then load the tracked spools into the correct AMS or external slots. Pre-sliced files must match the model they were sliced for. Being able to connect does not mean an arbitrary sliced file is compatible.

MQTT status/control: TCP 8883. FTPS file transfer: TCP 990, plus the passive data connections negotiated by the printer. Camera: TCP 322 for the cataloged X1 models; 6000 for P1/A1 models. Discovery: UDP 2021/1990 on the server's LAN. A working status connection does not confirm that file transfer and camera connections also work. If a bridged container cannot discover printers, add the printer by IP address. You can also use the supplied Linux host-network configuration. See Troubleshooting. X1-family cameras use RTSP, which the current application does not relay. Those models can connect for status/production while their camera view remains unavailable. P1/A1 snapshot cameras are supported.
Use Printers for the fleet list and open a printer for its camera, current job, hardware, feed units, maintenance, profiles, and recent activity.

Connection status and print status are separate. If a printer disconnects, OpenFarm still keeps its Not ready state. Ready: no active print is reported, and the printer takes jobs. Printing / Paused: an active print is running or paused. Not ready: the printer takes no job until you mark it ready. It becomes Not ready when a print ends (the plate is not confirmed clear) or when you mark it not ready. Offline: the server cannot currently reach the printer. Check the printer-reported state and alerts as well as OpenFarm's status. Camera images are snapshots refreshed while visible, not a recording archive.
Remove the finished or failed print. Inspect the bed and material path. Choose Mark ready. The printer becomes available for queued work. A compatible job can then start automatically.

To keep a Ready printer from taking jobs, for example for a nozzle swap, a bad spool or a repair, open it and choose Mark not ready. It stays Not ready, also after a reconnect or a restart, until you choose Mark ready. Queued work waits. Use the same permission as Mark ready. A printer that is printing cannot be marked not ready: it becomes Not ready by itself when its print ends.

Use Edit to change the name, connection settings, and build plate. Changing connection information triggers verification. The build plate is a check, not a slicing setting. A job goes only to a printer whose plate matches the file's plate. A ready printer with no plate selected shows Needs setup in the fleet list, on the dashboard, and on its page. It takes no jobs until you select a plate. See When profiles apply. A last-known nozzle value can remain visible while offline; production needs confirmation from the current connection. See Printer matching when the displayed size seems correct but a job is blocked.

Removal requires the corresponding permission and confirmation. Do not remove a printer to pause its queue. Resolve active work first. If you remove a printer with an open tracked print, OpenFarm records that print as failed. Historical print records remain available.
OpenFarm connects to the U1's existing Moonraker API over HTTP and WebSocket on port 7125. No extra agent is installed on the printer.

Put the OpenFarm server on a network that can reach the U1. Open Printers → Add printer. Select the discovered U1. For manual entry, enter its IP address with brand Snapmaker, model U1. Enter a name. If the printer requires an API key, enter it. Add the printer. OpenFarm reads the serial number from the printer and verifies its identity. Discovery uses mDNS on UDP 5353. If discovery finds no printer, you can still connect manually. DHCP can assign a saved IP address to a different U1. If its serial number does not match, OpenFarm keeps the printer offline. Correct the saved IP address.

Use OrcaSlicer for U1 production; Bambu Studio does not provide U1 presets. Select the supported high-temperature build plate. The U1 appears with four toolhead slots T1–T4. Load tracked spools into their actual slots. Each required filament must be on a head with the nozzle size the part needs. Heads can have different nozzle sizes; a preset at one diameter does not make every head compatible. OpenFarm uploads G-code, configures the tool-to-head mapping, and starts the print through Moonraker. A successful connection check does not confirm that every print operation works on your firmware version. The chamber camera requires HTTP access to the printer on port 80. OpenFarm keeps the camera awake while it monitors the printer. If a start request loses its response, OpenFarm waits for printer telemetry instead of sending the start again. Check the printer before you retry an unconfirmed print.

Review the outcome and object-skipping guide before you use partial plates or live exclusions. OpenFarm can count compatible standby stock toward the filament available for a print. Confirm that the U1's physical auto-replenish settings can use that stock.
OpenFarm uses its hardware catalog to select the printer connection software. Only models in this catalog are supported. A similar model is not automatically compatible.

Brand Models Connection Bambu Lab X1, X1 Carbon (X1C), X1E, P1P, P1S, A1, A1 mini (A1MINI) Direct LAN, access code required. Snapmaker U1 Moonraker over LAN; API key when required by the printer. System Simulation Software simulator for development, not physical hardware. This list follows PrinterModelCatalog in the codebase. Newer Bambu models are not implicitly supported. Camera support is separate: P1/A1 snapshot cameras and the U1 HTTP camera are supported. X1-family RTSP relay is not implemented in the current application.

Make the printer reachable from the OpenFarm server, even if you use the web UI from another machine. Reserve its LAN address where possible. Prepare Bambu LAN access or Snapmaker Moonraker access. Match the physical nozzle and build plate to production configuration. If discovery does not find a printer, use manual entry on Add printer. Discovery needs local broadcast or multicast traffic. A direct connection by IP address can still work when discovery is unavailable.
Backfill repeatedly prints whole plates until you pause or remove the entry. It uses compatible printers that are available after jobs with fixed quantities.

Open a part or assembly's Print flow and choose Continuous. Submit the entry, then manage it from Queue. By default, the entry uses one printer at a time. The entry remains visible even when it has no current jobs. You can limit how many printers it uses at once or pin it to one printer. You can also pause, resume, refresh, or remove it.

For assembly backfill, OpenFarm saves the number of each printed part needed for one assembly set. It compares these quantities with completed units and units already allocated to queued or running work. It gives priority to the eligible part furthest behind the proportions needed for the next complete set. If one part cannot print, this balancing limits excess production of the other parts. Failed and cancelled jobs do not count as completed output. Each selected part must still match a ready printer.

Pause blocks new dispatches and retries. It does not physically cancel an already running print. Refresh uses the assembly's current bill of materials (BOM). It replaces old requirements, cancels unsent jobs, and starts a new balancing period. Running prints remain linked to the original assembly recipe. Remove cancels unsent work and retains running prints and history. Backfill uses the current part file until OpenFarm prepares and sends a job. Changing a part file alone does not require an assembly recipe refresh. For an order with a fixed quantity and a defined end, use a run.

Open Job diagnosis on the job page, or select the blocking status in the queue row. The dialog checks current requirements for each printer. It shows the results and links to the settings you need to change.

Check What to verify Availability Printer is reachable, not busy, and has been cleared when required. Assignment A pinned job can use only its selected printer. Queue position and preference are separate from compatibility. Nozzle Reports from the current connection confirm the required diameter on every head and feed path the job uses. Target model Pre-sliced files match their declared target model. Material Required filament is physically loaded and registered as an active tracked spool. Identity The loaded spool matches the selected production color variant or the material and color requirements saved for the job. File and profiles The file must name the destination printer's model and the plate on its bed. All jobs need filament-profile assignments for loaded spools. If a job needs slicing, each filament preset must have a compatible match in the job's pinned slicer catalog. Build plate A required slicing plate is selected and compatible. Stock Known estimated use plus the fixed 10% margin fits available compatible stock.

For a 120 g estimate, the initial check requires 132 g, including the 10% margin. Compatible standby spools in the same AMS or configured reloader can contribute stock for continuation. An external spool by itself supplies only its own stock. Standby reloader slots do not count as separate active material choices. Unknown need does not block the stock check. After slicing, OpenFarm checks again using the generated file's exact grams. If it no longer fits, nothing is sent. Load more stock or correct a measured spool weight, then reevaluate.

Use When profiles apply to distinguish settings used to slice a new file from profiles checked for an already-sliced file. Pre-sliced jobs do not apply your current process and filament settings to existing toolpaths. A saved nozzle size from an offline printer is not current confirmation. Reconnect the printer and wait for a fresh nozzle report. Then check the filament assignments for that hardware and nozzle size. Changing the farm default does not change an existing part's saved slicer and version. If slicing is needed, a profile missing from that slicer's catalog can block the job. A user preset from another slicer can also block it. A similar name in another catalog is not enough.

Last attempt failed reports an error after the job passed compatibility checks, such as slicing or file transfer. Inspect the reason and server logs. Repeated dispatch failures use a growing retry delay. Opening or refreshing diagnosis is read-only and does not itself dispatch the job.
A completed printer command is not always a verified count of good output. Inspect the physical plate before confirming quantities or clearing the bed.

For a fixed target of units or sets, OpenFarm can select a partial final plate if the file has reliable object identifiers. Every recognized printable object instance counts as one unit. Modifiers, supports, and shared purge structures are not extra units. The job's object controls show whether live skipping is available. OpenFarm needs supported object identifiers that match the file used for the active print. A reliable object count alone is not enough. For example, raw Bambu G-code can contain object counts but lack the identifier table needed to skip objects. Prefer a labeled sliced 3MF for that workflow. Object exclusions use native Bambu or U1 commands. Verify firmware behavior on your hardware before depending on partial plates. Purge and shared structures may still print.

Output can remain unverified if object-skip confirmation is missing or the print ended during a connection interruption. Inspect the actual plate before you use Confirm produced units. Until you confirm the output, OpenFarm can block replacement or write-off actions for that completed attempt. Failed and cancelled attempts conservatively record zero produced units. Their material estimates can still count consumed filament.

Requeue missing units creates a replacement for the unresolved shortfall, retaining the original production snapshot. Write off missing units accepts the remaining loss without calling it produced stock. These operations preserve the original attempt and prevent resolving the same loss twice. Existing legacy whole-plate jobs may offer Requeue plate.

If OpenFarm cannot confirm a start request that uses object controls, it does not automatically send the request again. Check the printer first. The print might have started despite the network failure. If the printer is ready and the bed is clear, use Confirm print did not start. This cancels the attempt so you can requeue it.
documents.s: When the start acknowledgement is uncertain

documents.t: For sent jobs, downloads use the saved file prepared for that job. OpenFarm does not slice it again with current settings. For Bambu printers, the start request specifies the initial object exclusions. If you print the downloaded file outside OpenFarm, apply those exclusions again. U1 downloads already include their initial exclusion commands. Filament use remains an estimate that includes purge and extrusion before observed skips. It is not simply proportional to good-unit counts.
The queue holds physical plate attempts. You can print directly from a part or assembly without creating a production run.

Open a part and choose Print. Set the number of whole plates with − and +, check the units, time, and filament in the footer, and choose Queue n plates. For an assembly's direct Print flow, set whole-plate counts per component; zero skips a component. The Print dialog also sets: Plates or Continuous: Continuous turns the print into continuous backfill. Printer: Automatic uses any matching printer. A chosen printer pins the jobs to it, and the jobs wait for that printer. The list shows the live state of each printer. Position: Bottom adds the jobs after all waiting jobs. Top adds them before all waiting jobs. Filament (parts only): select a color, any color of one filament, or any color of the material for each requirement. The material stays the part's material. The jobs show the choice as a job override. Choose the reset button to use the part's filament again. For an exact unit target or complete assembly sets, use Runs. For repeat production during idle capacity, use Continuous backfill. Ready printers may start A queued job can start automatically on a compatible ready printer. Before you send work to the queue, check the physical bed and material path.

Open Queue and use its status tabs and part-name search. A job page shows the printer, production inputs, matched profiles, outcome, file, and available actions. Each printer shows progress while OpenFarm prepares and uploads its file. Physical printing starts separately. Queue ordering affects selection among eligible jobs. Compatibility is a separate decision: a job near the top may remain blocked while a later compatible job runs.

The row action menu shows the operations available for that job: Move to top changes waiting priority. Pin to printer restricts the job to one printer. Unpin restores automatic assignment. Remove job cancels unsent work after confirmation. Pinning does not bypass matching. A pinned job waits if its printer is busy, offline, missing material, or incompatible. Open the blocking status or Job diagnosis for details.

Pause, resume, and cancel are offered only for eligible jobs and accounts with explicit remote-control permission. Confirm the physical outcome after a stop. Printer-started prints are tracked separately from OpenFarm-dispatched jobs when observable. They can have incomplete file or spool information and do not become queued demand or run progress automatically.
A run groups an order or batch with fixed quantities. Use it to track progress and confirm completion. Direct queue jobs do not require a run.

Open Runs → Add run. Use Add part or assembly under Items to make. For a part, choose whole Plates or a Unit target. For an assembly, enter complete Sets. Choose automatic assignment or a specific printer for each line. Review required units, planned plates, and estimates. Enter the run details. Submit using Add run. The run's jobs appear in Queue. OpenFarm checks the plan again when you submit it. If library inputs changed during planning, refresh the plan and review the updated quantities before submitting again.

Suppose five assembly sets need two brackets each and the part contains six brackets per plate. The total is ten brackets: one job targets six and another targets four. Partial plates require reliable identifiers for complete printable units and a file that supports the required object selection. A quantity estimate alone is insufficient. If OpenFarm cannot verify safe selection, it blocks the operation. See Outcomes and recovery. Parts requested in Plates remain whole-plate jobs. Continuous backfill also schedules whole plates.

Open the run to see its lines, plate states, produced output, and unresolved shortfalls. Failed or cancelled attempts remain separate from their replacements in the history. Inspect output before confirming unknown quantities. Use Requeue missing units to replace an unresolved shortfall. Use Write off missing units to accept the loss. Available close and completion actions depend on the run's progress and unresolved work. Cancelling a run does not erase prints that already happened. Jobs with fixed quantities keep the source inputs saved when queued. OpenFarm still checks current printer settings and loaded spools before sending each job. Creating a plan does not reserve a printer configuration or its stock.
OpenFarm is developed in the getopenfarm/openfarm repository. Use its issue tracker for bugs and feature requests.

Include these details: Application version or image tag. Installation method. Affected printer model and firmware version. Steps to reproduce the problem. Expected result and actual error. For a job problem, include its matching diagnosis. State whether you printed directly, created a run, or used backfill. Provide a small sample file only if you can share it. Before sharing logs or configuration, remove access codes, API tokens, signing keys, passwords, and personal data.

Use Edit this page to propose a documentation change. Guides live in docs/content/; navigation order lives in docs/sidebars.ts. Follow the local docs workflow and build before opening a pull request. Describe the current product behavior and use the UI's actual action names. Keep future ideas and implementation notes in dev-notes/ so operators can follow the guides without mistaking planned work for a shipped feature. Use short, active sentences and consistent technical terms. Explain unfamiliar OpenFarm terms and give each numbered step one main action. Keep commands, interface labels, technical limits, and behavior exceptions accurate.
Open the affected printer or job page and read the error. Change one relevant setting at a time, then check the result.

If ORIGIN uses HTTPS, sign in through that hostname. Direct HTTP LAN access cannot send Secure refresh cookies. Route /api and /hubs through the same hostname. Confirm that the configured origin has no path other than / and no query. An existing account's password is not changed by editing Seed__AdminPassword. Ask another administrator to reset it. See Accounts.

For local development, check that ConnectionStrings__Default includes a password and matches the database user and port. dev.sh does not load Compose .env files. PostgreSQL checks authentication before it runs migrations. Recreating tables does not fix incorrect credentials. For Docker, initialization variables do not change passwords in an existing volume. Check the original credentials and keep the volume's data. If a PostgreSQL service already uses port 5432, resolve the conflict before starting the supplied host-network configuration.

Discovery happens on the server's LAN. The browser's network does not control it. Check Bambu UDP 2021/1990 or U1 mDNS UDP 5353, as applicable. Also check the host and container network settings. Bridged containers might not receive multicast traffic. If a direct connection works, enter the printer's IP address manually.

Check power, the IP address, DHCP reservation, credentials, and model support. Then check the relevant Bambu or U1 ports. Status, file transfer, and camera use separate connections. A U1 serial mismatch can indicate that DHCP reassigned the IP address. X1-family camera views are unavailable because the current app has no RTSP relay; opening the camera port does not enable that feature. If all browser live updates stop together, check WebSockets for /hubs/farm and sign in again if the browser session expired.
documents.s: Printer is offline or a camera is stale

documents.t: Open Job diagnosis and work through Printer matching. Check bed clearance, printer assignment, confirmed nozzle, loaded tracked spool and color, profiles, and plate. Known estimated use must fit the available stock with the 10% margin. A printer-reported material alone is not a registered spool. An offline remembered nozzle is not current confirmation. Pinning does not bypass either check.

Check Settings → Slicing defaults and the installed profile catalogs. Confirm the part's saved slicer and version, then check each filament's assignment for the printer model and nozzle size. For local development, run ./dev.sh slicers and ./dev.sh ingest. U1 production needs an OrcaSlicer selection and compatible U1 presets. Bambu Studio does not provide those presets. If slicing is needed, each selected profile must have a compatible match in the pinned slicer's catalog. A similar name in another catalog is not enough. A user preset from another slicer also blocks slicing.

You can save a project 3MF without estimates. Missing time or filament weight remains unknown. STL and geometry-only 3MF files are refused: save the model as a project from OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio. Review the required material and nozzle fields, then finish the file review. If you correct the source file or quantity, reprocess the part. See Parts.
documents.s: Upload has no estimate or is incomplete

documents.t: The file must contain reliable object identifiers. Raw Bambu G-code can have object counts without the table needed to skip objects. Before using Confirm produced units, inspect the physical plate. If the start result is uncertain, check the printer before using Confirm print did not start. See Recovery.
documents.s: Partial plate or output confirmation is blocked

documents.t: Check Action required entries, the spool assignment, remaining weight, and file estimates. A missing deduction does not mean no filament was used. If necessary, correct the weight from a measurement or record usage manually. Do not deduct the same usage twice. Blank prices leave costs partial.
